chunks: And whatever is narrated from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, I have narrated it from my father, and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim. And I have also narrated it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with him - from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to the author's father, a key narrator)

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muawiyah ibn Hakim's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs this passage to demonstrate the reliability of his own transmission (tadlis) of narrations from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, a key companion of Imam al-Sadiq. By citing two independent chains—one through his father and another through the prominent scholar Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar—he reinforces the authenticity of the isnad within the Usuli tradition. This method highlights the rigorous standards of hadith verification in Shia scholarship, ensuring that the narrator's reports are not isolated but corroborated by multiple scholarly lineages.
